title: When Should a Medical Image Classifier Abstain? A Cross-Modality Benchmark of Selective Prediction
description:
Code, logit bundles and results for a cross-modality benchmark of abstention (selective prediction) scores on medical image classifiers.

Eight scores are compared - maximum softmax probability, predictive entropy, temperature scaling, the top-1/top-2 margin, Monte-Carlo dropout, deep ensembles, and two split-conformal variants scored by prediction-set size (LAC and adaptive prediction sets) - across twelve MedMNIST 2D subsets covering eleven diagnostic modalities, with three random seeds per subset at 28x28 and two seeds at 128x128 on five subsets.

For every score the benchmark reports a post-hoc operating point and a deployable one whose threshold is fixed on the validation split, and it quantifies how far validation-calibrated thresholds and conformal quantiles miss their targets on test. Every number in the accompanying manuscript can be recomputed on CPU from the released logit bundles; the repository also contains the scripts that re-run the full training grid on a free GPU tier, the raw run logs, and the figures.
